        Graded against every 2026 MLB pitch of the same type, thrown with the same hand to the same batter side. Whiff+ of 100 is league average. Runs/100 is run value per 100 pitches versus league; positive saved runs. Location view: Zone% is the share of pitches in the strike zone, Chase% is the swing rate on pitches outside it, and in-zone whiff% is misses on swings at strikes, each shown against league. Velo is average release speed in mph. IVB is induced vertical break and HB is horizontal break, both in inches; positive HB breaks toward the pitcher’s arm side. xwOBAcon is expected damage on balls in play; negative is better for the pitcher, and it is grayed out under 20 balls in play. Pitches thrown fewer than 10 times to a side or in a count are left off. In the count table, usage is the share of his pitches in that count, and gray marks fewer than 30 swings.

        Sort by

        Pronators naturally turn the hand over at release, so changeups, sinkers and splitters come easier. Supinators naturally get to the side of the ball, so sweepers, curves and cutters come easier. This is a coaching rule of thumb, not a law.

        Grip notes are general starting points, not any one pitcher's grip. Work them out with a coach and a TrackMan or Rapsodo.

        Glossary

        Every term used on the site

        Results

        Usage
        How often a pitcher throws a pitch, as a share of all his pitches to that batter side.
        Whiff%
        Swings and misses divided by total swings.
        Whiff+
        Whiff% compared with league average for the same pitch type, throwing hand and batter side. 100 is average; 120 means 20% more misses.
        Run value
        How much each pitch changed the expected runs in the inning, from Statcast. Shown per 100 pitches against league average. Positive means it saved runs.
        xwOBAcon
        Expected damage on balls in play, built from exit velocity and launch angle. Lower is better for the pitcher. Shown against league average.
        Hard-hit%
        Share of balls in play hit 95 mph or harder.

        Location

        Zone%
        Share of pitches in the strike zone.
        Chase%
        How often hitters swing at a pitch outside the zone. The clearest sign a pitch fools people.
        In-zone whiff%
        Misses on swings at strikes. A pitch that gets these beats hitters even when they know it's coming.

        Movement and shape

        Velo
        Average release speed, in mph.
        IVB
        Induced vertical break: how much a pitch rises or drops compared with a pitch thrown with no spin, in inches.
        HB
        Horizontal break, in inches. Arm side means toward the pitcher's throwing arm (sinkers, changeups); glove side means away from it (sliders, sweepers).
        Off fastball
        How much slower a pitch is than the pitcher's main fastball, in mph.
        Pitch shape
        A group of pitches that move alike, such as a sweeper or a vertical slider, defined by velocity and break. See Pitch Shapes.
        Pitch comps
        The three closest pitches in MLB by velocity and movement, same throwing hand and pitch type.

        Arm and delivery

        Arm angle
        The angle of the arm at release, in degrees, from Statcast body tracking. 0° is straight sideways and 90° is straight up.
        Arm slots
        Submarine below 0°, sidearm 0–15°, low three-quarters 15–30°, three-quarters 30–45°, high three-quarters 45–60°, over the top 60°+. A rough guide.
        Pronator / supinator
        How a pitcher's hand naturally moves at release. Pronators turn it over, which helps changeups and sinkers. Supinators get to the side of the ball, which helps sweepers and curves.

        Flags

        Underused weapon
        Whiff+ 120 or higher, run value +1.0 or better, and thrown less than 25% of the time.
        Misses bats, still gets hurt
        Whiff+ 120 or higher, but run value −1.0 or worse.
        Below league average
        Run value −1.5 or worse.
        Heavy use, below average
        Thrown 25% of the time or more, with run value below zero.
        Hit hard on contact
        20+ balls in play and xwOBAcon .040 or more above league.
        Small sample
        Fewer than 30 swings, so the pitch isn't graded yet.

        Counts and changes

        Ahead / Even / Behind
        Ahead means more strikes than balls (0-1, 0-2, 1-2); behind means more balls than strikes.
        What changed since 2025
        New or dropped pitch, usage up or down 10+ points, velo up or down 1.5+ mph, or 2.5+ inches of new break. An arm slot change is 4°+.

        Teams

        Staff run value
        Every pitcher's run value on a staff, weighted by pitches thrown.
        Pitching payroll
        Combined salary of the pitchers on the current roster, from Spotrac.

        About

        Pitching analysis and tools

        Ben Kafka

        I work in ticket sales for the Brooklyn Cyclones at Maimonides Park and write pitching analysis for Pitcher List's Going Deep section. I also consult independently for a junior college program, working with its TrackMan data.

        Kafkaesque Baseball started as one question: is a pitcher using his pitches the right way? It grew into a tool that answers that for every pitcher in MLB. I designed the analysis and built it in Python with pybaseball, learning the language as I went and working with Claude as a coding partner. Every method, threshold and limit is written out in the notebook.

        StatcastpybaseballPython (learning)MLB Stats API
        How it works
        1. Every 2026 pitch. 716,792 regular-season pitches from Statcast, plus 2025 for year-over-year changes.
        2. Graded against exact peers. Each pitch is compared only to the same pitch type, thrown with the same hand to the same batter side, on whiffs, run value, contact quality and location.
        3. Flags where usage and results don't match. Underused weapons, pitches that miss bats but still get hurt, pitches that get hit hard.
        4. Written in plain English. Every card says what makes the pitcher nasty and what his biggest strength is.
